CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. Figure 5. — Anxiety Website Layout # Result To measure the classification performance, we have used the term Precision, Accuracy, Recall and F1-score. ## Precision Precision (positive predictive value) is the ratio of relevant positive observations to the total retrieved positive observations. (34) ## Recall Recall (Known as Sensitivity) - Recall is the ratio of relevant positive observations among all observations in actual class - yes. ## Accuracy Accuracy - In any measurement of performance, accuracy is a ratio between relevant observations and the total observations. We can say our model is best if we've high accuracy. Accuracy may be a great measure but only when values of false positive and false negatives are almost same of symmetric datasets. ## F1 score F1 score - Weighted average of precision and recall is called F1-score. Therefore, F1-score consider both false positives and false negatives. Naturally it is not as easy to achieve as accuracy, however if there is an uneven class distribution F1 is generally more useful than accuracy. (35) In our case, we see that in the support column, more than 60 percent of our test subjects noted that they are depressed, about 25-30% said they are addicted to internet and the rest are anxious. Accuracy only works better when the data is even, but that is not our case. So, our standard of efficiency should be the F1-score. We achieved accuracy, precision and F1-score up to 80 percent using SVM (Table II). So, KNN gave us the better accuracy and precision with the current dataset that we have. However, in future we will apply different types of decision tree methods to get better accuracy. The weighted average of our f1-score using KNN (Table 2) is 83 which is an acceptable result and better than f1 score of SVM. Hence, we decided to use KNN for our framework. ## Limitation One of the limitations of the exercise was limited number of features. Few specific special features were selected during feature engineering step to build the model and to fasten the process. Also, another limitation was sample data. The overall sample data was in lower base due to pandemic situation ## Discussion The purpose of the paper was to detect the physiological disorder of university students during this Covid-19 time. Two different machine learning methods were used to detect the disorders. First, we chose SVM as our machine learning technique since it looked like the more feasible choice. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. In our case, our classes are quite easily separable and that is a precondition for KNN to provide ## Conclusion Proper use of machine learning and modification of some of the algorithms may produce satisfactory result in determining mental disorder given a complete and information rich dataset. The Implementation part above shows that our model yields satisfactory result, and the precision is also reasonable. The algorithm we used on our dataset can be tweaked and twitched further for better result in the future. About the dataset, our data is one dimensional as all our test subjects were students. So, there are room for improvement. The more dimension that we can add in our dataset, the tougher the calculation would have been, but at the same time, the result could have been more precise. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. Two different machine learning methods were used to detect the disorders. First, we chose SVM as our machine learning technique since it looked like the more feasible choice. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. In our case, our classes are quite easily separable and that is a precondition for KNN to provide ## Conclusion Proper use of machine learning and modification of some of the algorithms may produce satisfactory result in determining mental disorder given a complete and information rich dataset. As we gave precedence in detecting target value out of the given input, making a desktop interface, and connecting external websites for the first step as self-help was secondary in our eyes. This can further be improved given enough time, adequate study on virtual CBT, manpower and willpower. We would also need specialist on CBT who can guide us through our interface making process to ensure accurate helps that can be done for the people. But for the first step to wellness, we think we have given our users enough chance to further study on their probable condition which may lead to their betterment. Finally, the final step of this project would be to publish it on cloud platform being a one stop, cross platform solution for people with behavioral disorder. ## References 1. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. Two different machine learning methods were used to detect the disorders. First, we chose SVM as our machine learning technique since it looked like the more feasible choice. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. As we gave precedence in detecting target value out of the given input, making a desktop interface, and connecting external websites for the first step as self-help was secondary in our eyes. This can further be improved given enough time, adequate study on virtual CBT, manpower and willpower. We would also need specialist on CBT who can guide us through our interface making process to ensure accurate helps that can be done for the people. But for the first step to wellness, we think we have given our users enough chance to further study on their probable condition which may lead to their betterment. Finally, the final step of this project would be to publish it on cloud platform being a one stop, cross platform solution for people with behavioral disorder. ## References 1. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. The algorithm we used on our dataset can be tweaked and twitched further for better result in the future. About the dataset, our data is one dimensional as all our test subjects were students. Figure 5. — Anxiety Website Layout # Result To measure the classification performance, we have used the term Precision, Accuracy, Recall and F1-score. ## Precision Precision (positive predictive value) is the ratio of relevant positive observations to the total retrieved positive observations. (34) ## Recall Recall (Known as Sensitivity) - Recall is the ratio of relevant positive observations among all observations in actual class - yes. ## Accuracy Accuracy - In any measurement of performance, accuracy is a ratio between relevant observations and the total observations. We can say our model is best if we've high accuracy. Accuracy may be a great measure but only when values of false positive and false negatives are almost same of symmetric datasets. ## F1 score F1 score - Weighted average of precision and recall is called F1-score. Therefore, F1-score consider both false positives and false negatives. Naturally it is not as easy to achieve as accuracy, however if there is an uneven class distribution F1 is generally more useful than accuracy. (35) In our case, we see that in the support column, more than 60 percent of our test subjects noted that they are depressed, about 25-30% said they are addicted to internet and the rest are anxious. Accuracy only works better when the data is even, but that is not our case. So, our standard of efficiency should be the F1-score. We achieved accuracy, precision and F1-score up to 80 percent using SVM (Table II). Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (vCBT). ## Specific Behavioral Disorder chosen for this research * Depression - Depression is a very common and serious behavioral disorder. Depression is highly prevailed amongst the population hence considered as very common (14). Depression takes away all the pleasure of personal to social life ranging from eating, sleeping, resting, playing, studying, mental capacity to analyze things, entertaining etc. (15). * Anxiety - Anxiety itself is not a natural behavioral disorder as every living being feel anxiety which is standard and often can be seemed like healthy emotion (14). However, when the feeling gets more frequent and can unearth the person with highly disproportionate means that disrupt regular day-to-day life, then it can be considered as a mental disorder that needs to be looked after. Therefore, if a person often feels unbalanced levels of anxiety, it might become a health disorder (16). Usually the diagnoses are as follows: excessive nervousness, fear, apprehension and feeling of extreme worry. These feelings may alter how emotion is processed and thus, effecting external behavior which may cause physical symptoms. Minor anxiety might be elusive and disturbing, but in case of severe disorder, it may extremely affect a person's everyday living. ## Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a helping process to overcome person's emotional and intellectual experience: how they are feeling and what they think about the problem they have sought for help. CBT is a hands-on, practical method of psychotherapy that is implemented for a smaller period to reach to the goal faster and approach to self-healing/thinking approach so that the patient alters his mental situation by his own core beliefs. The primary goal is to change how a person thinks or behaves that causes the difficulty or mental block. It is used to treat a wide range of issues in a person's life. CBT aims to change one's attitude and behavior towards life by focusing on the feelings, norms, beliefs, and attitudes (20). ## Steps in CBT Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is customized to cater patient's definite condition. CBT process, techniques and required steps need to be understood for successful implementation (21). The steps in CBT are given below: 1. Identify disturbing circumstances or situations of life and define focus areas. 2. Awareness of feelings, sentiments, and beliefs. Usually, patients are prescribed to record of every thought. (3) Identify negative or erroneous thought process. Advised to be concerned about every physical and behavioural responses to every circumstances. (4) Restructure negative or erroneous thinking process which takes time and patience. (5) CBT is usually treated as a short-rang therapy which last about 10 to 20 sessions. ## Effectiveness of CBT CBT facilitates positive changes in person's life. It is a psychotherapeutic approach of helping someone to come to terms with and workout solution to their problems. However, they vary based on the approach used and underpinning model according to the category of disorder. Depression – One of the Australian cohort study identified that CBT and pharmacological treatments had reasonable impact on Depression. (22) When suffering from severe depression, one requires long-term treatment strategies that involve either medication or psychological therapy. (23) Anxiety - A meta-analysis by Kristin Mitte evaluated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and pharmacological therapy in treating comprehensive anxiety disorder. There were 869 patients involved in that analysis. The analysis includes thirteen studies which compares CBT to regulate the groups and six comparing CBT with pharmacotherapy. She concluded that, the present meta-analysis results specify CBT is a highly effective treatment that reduces the key signs of anxiety as well as the related depressive symptoms. As a result, life quality improves subsequently. (24) Internet Addiction - Addictive behavior has a wide range of variety starting from drug abuse to the minimum of mobile phone addiction and each addiction is detrimental in their own way and cannot be undermined. Professor of Psychology, Charles Scherbaum casually divided 73 opioid-dependent patients into two groups. He gave methadone to the first group with 20 weeks of group CBT. (25) On the other hand, second group received methadone and treatment as usual i.e counselling. Neither group had a different rate of negative urine tests after weeks of treatment. However, the CBT group had a lower rate of positive urine drug tests after months of follow-up. Figure 5. — Anxiety Website Layout # Result To measure the classification performance, we have used the term Precision, Accuracy, Recall and F1-score. ## Precision Precision (positive predictive value) is the ratio of relevant positive observations to the total retrieved positive observations. (34) ## Recall Recall (Known as Sensitivity) - Recall is the ratio of relevant positive observations among all observations in actual class - yes. ## Accuracy Accuracy - In any measurement of performance, accuracy is a ratio between relevant observations and the total observations. We can say our model is best if we've high accuracy. Accuracy may be a great measure but only when values of false positive and false negatives are almost same of symmetric datasets. ## F1 score F1 score - Weighted average of precision and recall is called F1-score. Therefore, F1-score consider both false positives and false negatives. Naturally it is not as easy to achieve as accuracy, however if there is an uneven class distribution F1 is generally more useful than accuracy. (35) In our case, we see that in the support column, more than 60 percent of our test subjects noted that they are depressed, about 25-30% said they are addicted to internet and the rest are anxious. Accuracy only works better when the data is even, but that is not our case. So, our standard of efficiency should be the F1-score. We achieved accuracy, precision and F1-score up to 80 percent using SVM (Table II). Table II. — Accuracy result using SVM | | Precision | Recall | F1-score | Support | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 0.86 | 0.90 | 0.88 | 60 | | 2 | 0.88 | 0.70 | 0.78 | 30 | | 3 | 0.38 | 0.50 | 0.43 | 10 | | **Accuracy** | | | | | | **Macro avg** | 0.71 | 0.70 | 0.70 | 100 | | **Weighted avg** | 0.82 | 0.80 | 0.80 | 100 | Table III. —Accuracy result using KNN | Type | Precision | Recall | F1-score | Support | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 0.93 | 0.90 | 0.92 | 62 | | 2 | 0.74 | 0.82 | 0.78 | 28 | | 3 | 0.44 | 0.40 | 0.42 | 10 | | Accuracy | | 0.83 | 100 | | Macro avg | 0.71 | 0.71 | 0.71 | 100 | | Weighted avg | 0.83 | 0.83 | 0.83 | 100 | good results; if KNN failed, then it would have pointed to the fact that the metric vector we have chosen does not produce separable classes and that is quite opposite to our dataset. So, KNN gave us the better accuracy and precision with the current dataset that we have. However, in future we will apply different types of decision tree methods to get better accuracy. The weighted average of our f1-score using KNN (Table 2) is 83 which is an acceptable result and better than f1 score of SVM. Hence, we decided to use KNN for our framework. ## Limitation One of the limitations of the exercise was limited number of features. Few specific special features were selected during feature engineering step to build the model and to fasten the process. Also, another limitation was sample data. The overall sample data was in lower base due to pandemic situation ## Discussion The purpose of the paper was to detect the physiological disorder of university students during this Covid-19 time. Two different machine learning methods were used to detect the disorders. First, we chose SVM as our machine learning technique since it looked like the more feasible choice. Using SVM, we had a precision and accuracy of about 60 percent at the start and we need to make a complete makeover of our dataset and normalized it to get the accuracy and precision up to 80 percent. As we were thinking about making a desktop app that takes input from an interface, we tried different approaches and we had to renormalize our data and made some major changes. We changed our model from SVM to KNN because the new normalized data set was best suited for KNN. SVM can easily separate dataset using decision planes, i.e. the basic SVM separate classes using linear hyperplanes but in the cases of different kernel, it will change the shape of decision plane. K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) works better than SVM. KNN can generate highly complex decision as the main driving issue is the raw training data. SVM uses a limited parametric estimate of the decision limit, which is fine if anyone prefer performance against processing speed ratio. In our case, our classes are quite easily separable and that is a precondition for KNN to provide ## Conclusion Proper use of machine learning and modification of some of the algorithms may produce satisfactory result in determining mental disorder given a complete and information rich dataset. The Implementation part above shows that our model yields satisfactory result, and the precision is also reasonable. The algorithm we used on our dataset can be tweaked and twitched further for better result in the future. About the dataset, our data is one dimensional as all our test subjects were students. So, there are room for improvement. The more dimension that we can add in our dataset, the tougher the calculation would have been, but at the same time, the result could have been more precise. work was identified as a risk factor for workplace suicide (Stack, 2001; Tiesman et al., 2015). In our previous study, we confirmed that major emotional problems like depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation were common among shift workers (Park et al., 2020). Another study reported that shift work increased work stress and that the risk of suicide was significantly increased when the quality of sleep was poor (Son and Lee, 2021). These results considered shift work as one of the major risk factors, but the question of which of the various factors affects the risk of suicide was not adequately addressed. ## 1.3. Purpose of this study With the continued development of machine learning, research using it is diversifying. Machine learning is useful when analyzing multiple predictors when there are nonlinear observation and interaction terms that are difficult to conceptualize theoretically and model in practice. This study attempted to predict suicidal ideation based on shift work patterns using machine learning techniques. For this purpose, a variety of variables from national health surveys conducted over several years were used as predictive variables. # 2. Methods ## 2.1. Participants This study used data from KHANES. The KHANES is a nationwide health and nutrition survey based on Article 16 of the National Health Promotion Act enacted in 1995. The health level, health behavior, and food and nutritional intake are representative and reliable statistics at the national level and through these data, help to establish health policy, such as setting and evaluating the goals of the National Health Promotion Plan and developing health promotion programs. Data for a span of 10 years were used: 2007–2013, 2015, 2017, and 2019. The 2014, 2016, and 2018 surveys did not include adult suicidal ideation, so they were excluded. All participants in KHANES provided written consent prior to the investigation so that their personal information could be used. This study included 45,386 adults aged 20 years or older who had been working for at least one year out of 10 years of survey data. Among them, a total of 43,095 people were analyzed, excluding 1391 people who did not answer their work type and 919 people who did not respond to questions related to suicidal ideation (Fig. 1). The Institutional Review Board of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency approved this study (2018-01-03-P-A). ## 2.2. Measurements ### 2.2.1. Assessment of work patterns We divided work types into day work and shift work. Shift work included evening work (14:00–24:00), night shift (21:00–08:00), regular day and night shift work, 24-h shift work, split work (more than two working hours per day), irregular shift work, and other forms of shift work. ### 2.2.2. Assessment for suicide Suicide was evaluated by asking questions about suicidal ideation over the past year. The evaluative question presented to study participants asked, “*During the past year, have you ever felt that you were willing to die?*” They were classified as having suicidal ideation if they answered yes, and if they answered no, they were classified as having no suicidal ideation. ### 2.2.3. Assessment for quality of life Quality of life can be divided into health-related quality of life (HRQOL) and non-health-related quality of life (NHRQOL) (Spilker, 1996). Health-related quality of life refers to areas of life that are directly affected by changes in health. Health, as defined by the WHO, is not simply the absence of disease, but complete physical, mental, and social well-being. In this study, EuroQol-5 Dimension (EQ-5D) was used as an HRQOL measurement tool. EQ-5D is a tool that can measure HRQOL as a utility and consists of five items which include mobility, self-care, normal activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression. The higher the total score, the higher the quality of life. ### 2.2.4. Assessment for stress The stress level is evaluated with close-ended questions on a four points Likert scale (How much stress do you feel in your daily life?). The participants answered four type of stress level; extremely, stressful, moderately and minimally. ## 2.3. Statistical analysis In this study, 19 analyzable variables thought to be related to suicidal ideation were selected and used. Missing values in some data were filled in using Predictive Mean Matching (PMM) from the Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) package of R statistical software. We performed the random forest (RF) and the k-nearest neighbors (KNN) classification algorithms. --- Figure 1. Among machine learning algorithms, RF is a method used to identify an optimal result by randomly combining the results by constructing multiple decision trees; RF is widely used because it is more accurate than decision trees. However, RF also has the disadvantage of losing the explanatory power of the variables included in the decision trees. A decision tree (DT) is one of the most widely used machine learning techniques for the purpose of classifying high-risk subjects. A decision tree is composed of decision nodes, branches, and leaves. It is divided into yes and no from the first question (Root Node), and the variable area is divided into two for each node, leading to the last terminal node. Finally, each divided tree is a set with the same tendency. Separation at each node can be said to have the highest explanatory, predictive power. Therefore, in this study, RF, a method with higher explanatory power, was performed first to evaluate the model suitability, followed by DT to present the explanatory power of each variable relative to suicidal ideation. Efforts are needed to reduce risk factors through administrative and policy interventions to manage workers' health by early screening. --- ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1. Shift work and health Shift work is defined as working outside the normal working hours of 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, with 15–25% of global workers working in shifts (Wickwire et al., 2017). Shift workers are exposed to artificial light at night, which causes their circadian rhythm to be disturbed (Fonken et al., 2013; Stevens et al., 2007). Light exposure at night can impair learning and memory abilities (Fonken et al., 2012) and may lead to neurodegeneration associated with Alzheimer's disease (Kim et al., 2018). Shift workers often complain of sleep disturbances or drowsiness during waking hours due to disturbances of the normal sleep-wake cycle. According to the Korean National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KHANES), 37.6% of workers get less than seven hours of sleep. Among them, sleep deprivation impacts 61.8% of shift workers (Yong et al., 2017). In addition, light pollution negatively impacts overall human health, including aging, metabolic processes, heart disease, diabetes, and mood disorders (Gangwisch, 2014; Hood et al., 2004; Stevens et al., 2007). Sleep is essential for humans to maintain physical and mental homeostasis by providing rest and stability. However, shift workers have no choice but to sleep at a different time than the body's circadian rhythm, resulting in poor sleep quality and sleep deprivation (Niu et al., 2011). Workers who complained of sleep disturbance were 2.8 times more likely to receive treatment (Daley et al., 2009) or prescription drugs for various health problems, including mental health problems, compared to those who did not (Haus and Smolensky, 2013; Kecklund and Axelsson, 2016). In the case of nurses, it can impact patient safety by reducing concentration and increasing fatigue during work, thus increasing the risk of various in-hospital accidents such as medication errors or malfunctions of medical devices (Wickwire et al., 2017; Yuan et al., 2011). As chronic circadian misalignment occurs, this social jet lag is known to have a negative effect on individual health, such as unhealthy eating habits, personality changes, metabolic disorders, and increased depression (Roenneberg et al., 2019). --- * Corresponding author at: Department of Psychiatry, Hanyang University Medical Center, 222-1, Wangsimni-ro, Seongdong-gu, Seoul 04763, Republic of Korea. Shift work and suicide A study of police officers discovered that depression, PTSD symptoms, and the type of work all increased suicidal ideation in female police officers (Violanti et al., 2008). Shift work was identified as a risk factor for workplace suicide (Stack, 2001; Tiesman et al., 2015). In our previous study, we confirmed that major emotional problems like depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation were common among shift workers (Park et al., 2020). Another study reported that shift work increased work stress and that the risk of suicide was significantly increased when the quality of sleep was poor (Son and Lee, 2021). These results considered shift work as one of the major risk factors, but the question of which of the various factors affects the risk of suicide was not adequately addressed. ## 1.3. Purpose of this study With the continued development of machine learning, research using it is diversifying. Machine learning is useful when analyzing multiple predictors when there are nonlinear observation and interaction terms that are difficult to conceptualize theoretically and model in practice. This study attempted to predict suicidal ideation based on shift work patterns using machine learning techniques. Assessment of work patterns We divided work types into day work and shift work. Shift work included evening work (14:00–24:00), night shift (21:00–08:00), regular day and night shift work, 24-h shift work, split work (more than two working hours per day), irregular shift work, and other forms of shift work. ### 2.2.2. Assessment for suicide Suicide was evaluated by asking questions about suicidal ideation over the past year. The evaluative question presented to study participants asked, “*During the past year, have you ever felt that you were willing to die?*” They were classified as having suicidal ideation if they answered yes, and if they answered no, they were classified as having no suicidal ideation. ### 2.2.3. Assessment for quality of life Quality of life can be divided into health-related quality of life (HRQOL) and non-health-related quality of life (NHRQOL) (Spilker, 1996). Health-related quality of life refers to areas of life that are directly affected by changes in health. Health, as defined by the WHO, is not simply the absence of disease, but complete physical, mental, and social well-being. In this study, EuroQol-5 Dimension (EQ-5D) was used as an HRQOL measurement tool. EQ-5D is a tool that can measure HRQOL as a utility and consists of five items which include mobility, self-care, normal activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression. The higher the total score, the higher the quality of life. ### 2.2.4. Assessment for stress The stress level is evaluated with close-ended questions on a four points Likert scale (How much stress do you feel in your daily life?). The participants answered four type of stress level; extremely, stressful, moderately and minimally. ## 2.3. The higher the total score, the higher the quality of life. ### 2.2.4. Among machine learning algorithms, RF is a method used to identify an optimal result by randomly combining the results by constructing multiple decision trees; RF is widely used because it is more accurate than decision trees. However, RF also has the disadvantage of losing the explanatory power of the variables included in the decision trees. A decision tree (DT) is one of the most widely used machine learning techniques for the purpose of classifying high-risk subjects. A decision tree is composed of decision nodes, branches, and leaves. It is divided into yes and no from the first question (Root Node), and the variable area is divided into two for each node, leading to the last terminal node. Finally, each divided tree is a set with the same tendency. Separation at each node can be said to have the highest explanatory, predictive power. Therefore, in this study, RF, a method with higher explanatory power, was performed first to evaluate the model suitability, followed by DT to present the explanatory power of each variable relative to suicidal ideation.
